relations.note: Medieval genealogy makes the Tuatha Dé descendants of Nemed.
The Tuatha Dé descend from Nemed through Iarbonel the Soothsayer.
Beothach belongs to the genealogical line connecting the Tuatha Dé with Nemed.

relations.myth: Training in the northern city of Falias
relations.note: Morfessa teaches the Tuatha Dé in Falias.

relations.myth: Training in the northern city of Gorias
relations.note: Esras teaches the Tuatha Dé in Gorias.

relations.myth: Training in the northern city of Findias
relations.note: Uiscias teaches the Tuatha Dé in Findias.

relations.myth: Training in the northern city of Murias
relations.note: Semias teaches the Tuatha Dé in Murias.
The Tuatha Dé defeat the Fir Bolg after negotiations over Ireland fail.

relations.myth: Bres’s reign and the Fomorian tribute
relations.note: Fomorian overlords exact produce and humiliating labor from the Tuatha Dé.
The Tuatha Dé defeat the Fomorian host through coordinated divine arts.
Later narratives make Manannán their counselor, protector, concealer, and distributor of dwellings.

relations.myth: The Sons of Míl invade Ireland
relations.note: The Tuatha Dé submit to Amergin’s judgment governing the Milesians’ second landing.

relations.myth: The Sons of Míl invade Ireland
relations.note: The Tuatha Dé negotiate and fight with the Sons of Míl, raising magical winds.
